Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has downplayed concerns about his team’s togetherness and insisted he is not worried about star striker Erling Haaland following downcast post-match interviews.

City had won 11 of their first 12 matches in all competitions this season but have suffered an alarming downturn in form, only winning two of their last seven games.

Talisman Haaland has also suffered a slump at the same time, scoring just one goal in five games, and cut a morose figure when he was interviewed after a battling 2-2 draw against Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday.

However, Maresca has insisted their poor run and the Norwegian’s demeanour are not cause for concern.

He noted: “I think Erling is a winner. It's normal that he's not happy when we don't win games but not just Erling, everyone.

Sources indicate that “Remember just a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch. You can write and think many different things.

In a recent development, “Erling is upset. I'm upset because we're not winning games. But this is our job, this is football. That's why I need to maintain the balance.

Industry observers note that “He's a nine. They live day by day for goals and winning games. If they don't score or win games they're upset. So I don't think that affects his game but for sure he's not happy not winning games, but everyone is on the same page.”.

It has been revealed that asked whether it has been business as usual in training, he noted: “He has been good. Yes, normal like since day one. Again, a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch, he was dancing in training. He's happy. It's normal that results affect the mood, that's why we need to win games.

“But I don't see any problem at all with Erling.”.

Industry observers note that the Italian insisted that “transition takes time” and added: “For me, it's completely normal, I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all. I understand that we need to win games because it's our business but for me, it's all normal.”.

Asked whether their string of poor results, which includes a 10-game run without a clean sheet, had affected players’ confidence, he said: “For sure, when you don't win games, it's not the ideal situation. But we won games at the beginning. We have also seven or eight fresh players that need to be used to winning games, so it's just a process.”.

City face another significant test as they visit league leaders Arsenal, who are six points ahead, on Sunday.

Maresca was insistent that City were not lacking in belief ahead of their trip to the defending champions, saying: “I think we have already shown this season that we are able to win notable games, to win away. I don't see any reason why we are not able to win there.”.

An in situ redox-converted molecule for all-perovskite tandem solar cells

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (593 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • All-perovskite tandem solar cells (TSCs) are gaining prominence due to their ability to surpass the efficiency limit of single-junction perovskite solar cells (PSCs)1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All-perovskite tandem solar cells (TSCs) are gaining prominence due to their ability to surpass the efficiency limit of single-junction perovskite solar cells (PSCs)1,2. However, the efficiency and stability of all-perovskite TSCs are limited by chemical instability at the hole transport layer/perovskite interface in the tin-lead (Sn-Pb) narrow-bandgap subcell, which introduces deep trap states from tin cations and promotes non-radiative recombination3-5. Here we incorporate a redox-converted molecule of p-aminobenzohydrazide (ABH) into poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) that neutralizes PSS acidity, heals Sn4+ defects, and generates a dipole passivation effect upon oxidation. During the preparation of Sn-Pb perovskites, ABH suppresses interfacial oxidation by reducing Sn4+ defects and converts to p-aminobenzaldehyde (ABD), which suppresses photogenerated hole-induced Sn2+ oxidation, aligning energy levels for efficient hole extraction. The in situ redox-converted molecule stabilizes the buried interface during both device fabrication and operation, reduces non-radiative recombination and enhances stability. The resulting narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb PSC achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.4% (certified 25.2%) with an open-circuit voltage of 0.92 V and a fill factor of 83.4%. Integrated into monolithic all-perovskite TSCs, the device delivers a PCE of 31.1% (certified 30.8%) together with enhanced thermal (ISOS-D-2I, 85 °C) and operational stability (ISOS-L-1I) under inert conditions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group.
  • The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.
  • It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group.

The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however Northern Ireland's draw against Hungary saw them top Group B2 and secure promotion to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The Republic of Ireland finished second in Group B3 and so will take part in a League A/B promotion play-off in March.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:.

They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

The remaining dates for the Nations League are:.

Quarter-finals first leg: 25-27 March.

Quarter-finals second leg: 28-30 March.

Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that this blog is now closed. Read below for more on these stories and all other things Germany on Monday, November 23.

Thank you for following our coverage of headlines from Germany on Monday, November 24.

The Federal President’s latest major trip takes him to Africa. Frank-Walter Steinmeier has just visited the Ivory Coast and is continuing on to Ghana and Kenya. His goal: to encourage more German companies to invest in Africa.

Recent findings suggest that frank-Walter Steinmeier has visited 31 African countries during his political career. Even as foreign minister, he traveled regularly to the continent; as federal president, he has made twelve trips so far.

From early on, he viewed Africa not only through the lens of development aid and humanitarian support, but also — much like former Chancellor Angela Merkel — as a market for the German economy that has been underutilized thus far. In 2015, as foreign minister in the Merkel administration, Steinmeier played a central role in the creation of the German-African Economic Summit.

On his current trip as well, Steinmeier is advocating for greater German engagement in Africa. In Abidjan, the capital of the Ivory Coast, following a meeting with Ivorian President Alassane Ouattara, he called on German companies to step outside their comfort zone and take greater advantage of the opportunities offered by the country and the continent.

The Ivory Coast is considered a location with growing potential. Despite its proximity to the Sahel region, which is plagued by terrorism, the country is relatively stable politically. The economy is growing by about six percent annually. Germany has more intensive trade relations with the Ivory Coast than with any other country in sub-Saharan Africa, and nowhere else in sub-Saharan Africa do so many people learn German — an advantage for German small and medium-sized enterprises — all of which both presidents emphasized very clearly during their meeting in Abidjan.

It has been revealed that up next, Steinmeier is scheduled to visit Accra, Ghana, for the sixth German-African Economic Summit, where more than 600 business representatives are expected to attend. As the summit’s initiator, the Federal President will open the event together with the host, Ghanaian President John Mahama. He will be accompanied by a ten-member business delegation representing industry, the financial sector, and energy consulting.

The Economic Summit is taking place at a time when Germany’s relations with African countries are undergoing fundamental changes. In light of geopolitical shifts, Africa is increasingly coming into focus as an economic and trade partner.

Recent findings suggest that the continent’s share of German foreign trade at the moment stands at just under 2%, or around €30 billion. At the same time, German exports to Africa are rising by at least 6% annually. And since Germany’s economy aims to reduce its dependence on China in the future, opportunities in Africa are growing.

From Ghana, Frank-Walter Steinmeier will travel on to Kenya, the final stop on his tour of Africa.

Environment Minister Carsten Schneider on Monday vowed that Germany will continue to move away from burning fossil fuels despite the failure of the COP31 declaration in Antalya, Turkey, this weekend.

Speaking at an event in Potsdam, Schneider mentioned: "We will clearly maintain our course on climate protection in Europe and Germany, but above all one that makes us independent of oil and gas because otherwise we are vulnerable to blackmail and our economic performance becomes extremely volatile.".

Schneider expressed disappointment less at the result of the two-week conference than its format, which he said was far more focussed on spectacle than substance.

Speaking of his vision for a format for future climate conferences, Schneider said: "Basically, I don't need so many people there. What I need are the relevant decision makers with whom I negotiate and make decisions.".

Although he voiced relief that the final document from the conference had not represented a step backwards — as well as stressing that some 30 countries had pledged to maintain the move away from fossil fuels — Schneider acknowledged that it had been nearly impossible to find consensus with Russia and Saudi Arabia at the table.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius urged calm over reports that Russia was planning to launch a nuclear-armed satellite into space as early as next month.

"First of ​all, ‌let's remain calm, because there are reports — that's true — but ‌it's ​not clear what kind of weapons these are, and the ​effect they might have depends, in ⁠turn, ​on where they ​are deployed," Pistorius told ​reporters in ‌Berlin.

Recent findings suggest that "Therefore, it's too early to ​speculate ⁠publicly about this. We are consulting ⁠internally ​and taking the necessary measures.".

German public broadcasters NDR and WDR and newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung first reported on the matter, which mentioned that internal intelligence reports circulated among NATO countries earlier this month said that Russia was ready to bring the alleged satellite, named Sputnik-S, out of storage in Moscow.

The reports said Russia may be planning to launch it as soon as December.

Nuclear weapons are banned in orbit by the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, of which Moscow is a signatory.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said not allowing Ukraine intoNATO in 2008 was a mistake.

At the2008 summit in Bucharest, Romania, German Chancellor Angela Merkel and French President Nicolas Sarkozy argued that they weren't ready to extend NATO membership to Ukraine.

US President George W. Bush said he was in favor of having Ukraine enter into NATO.

But both Germany and France said that that would hurt relations with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The NATO summit then decided that Ukraine would eventually join the alliance, but offered no timetable.

At a press conference on Monday, Merz was asked about whether he thinks the time was right to talk about Ukraine's membership in NATO.

To which Merz said, "If it [Ukraine] had become a member of NATO, this war could probably have been prevented.".

Merz meant Russia's war against Ukraine when he noted "this war" at the press conference after a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.

Angela Merkel defended her decision at the Bucharest summit as of 2024 as well, saying a large proportion of the Ukrainian population had opposed joining NATO at the time.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called on Russia to end its "dangerous provocations" after two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone crashed in Poland on Friday.

Merz delivered those remarks after having met with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in Berlin on Monday.

"Poland can count on our full solidarity. And if necessary, NATO will of course defend every inch of allied territory," Merz stated.

Merz said Europe and NATO must strengthen their defenses.

Drones have repeatedly strayed into NATO airspace in the year since Russia introduced its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

The incident also came at a time as Poland was hosting a two-week military exercise by Ukraine's allies.

German startup investments in fields such as robotics and defense are set to almost triple this year, a study noted on Monday.

The German Start-up Association and the Joachim Herz Foundation study predicted that investments in so-called "deep tech startups" will surge from just €2.9 billion ($3.17 billion) last year to 8.1 billion ($8.9 billion) this year.

The study described the rise as a "major success for Germany as a business location.".

"Deep tech" typically refers to developing cutting-edge technologies based on scientific research, such as AI, biotechnology and quantum computing.

A handful of massive fundraising rounds by firms including humanoid robot developer Neura Robotics,  AI drone maker Helsing and defense tech group Quantum Systems drove the investment boom.

The study also highlighted about 300 fresh deep tech startups are expected to be founded this year, a 40% rise compared with last year.

Newly found startups tend to be founded around economic hubs like Berlin and Hamburg, which are also home to leading universities and research institutes.

The study also highlighted challenges, including limited funding compared with their US counterparts and insufficient support to move startups from the laboratory to the real world.

Police in several locations across Germany reported large numbers of bomb threats targeting schools.

They remarked that while they were investigating the claims, they did not initially have reason to treat them as credible threats.

More than 400 schools in the southwestern state of Baden-Württemberg received threats, and more than 250 in Saxony-Anhalt received the emails, with several other regions also targeted on Monday morning.

Similar reports have also emerged to the north of Germany, in Denmark.

As in Germany, Danish police said they did not believe the threats were credible, "but they understandably create insecurity locally at the schools.".

Read more about the disruptive incidents that have targeted Europe in recent weeks.

Germany's Freie Wähler (Free Voters) party have chosen a upcoming chairman, weeks after their former front man Hubert Aiwanger unexpectedly passed away on November 4.

The party announced on Monday that Bavaria's Digital Affairs Fabian Mehring is to succeed Aiwanger both as party leader on the federal level and as one of two co-chairs of the Bavaria section of they party. The second state co-chair still needs to be decided.

Aiwanger was found dead in a Berlin hotel room at the age of 55 with no foul play suspected. He's been the party's defining figure for almost four decades, having led the Free Voters to substantial success, especially in Bavaria.

According to recent reports, the Free Voters are originally a grass roots party in Bavaria and sit on the conservative edge of the political spectrum. They've been in government in Bavaria as junior coaltion partners of the Christian Social Union (CSU), sister party to Chancellor Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

There are also changes in the Bavarian state government. Tobias Gotthardt is to take over as economy minister, while Environment Minister Thorsten Glauber is set to become deputy premier behind Bavaria state Premier Markus Söder. The appointments still require formal approval by party conventions.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has inisted that NATO was ready to defend itself in the face of potential Russian threats against any of its member states.

"We will always defend every inch of our NATO territory," Wadephul said at the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

His comments come after three Russian projectiles violated Polish airspace on Friday and crashed in the southeast of the country.

Wadephul is attending the NATO assembly in Berlin and DW has   a dedicated blog on those talks  where you can read all about how Russia's war in Ukraine is taking center stage for the defense alliance.

It has been revealed that A massive strike is underway in Germany hitting major car brands another manufacturing factors. Metal and electrical workers are demanding better pay ahead of upcoming wage talks later this week. The strike has been initiated by IG Metall, Germany’s biggest and most powerful union.

Famous car brands Mercedes and BMW  were affected as was an Opel plant, which is part of the international Stellantis group.

Recent findings suggest that the strikes began on Friday and are due to continue until Tuesday. Wage negotiations are then set to continue on Wednesday with another round of collective bargaining for some 3.7 million workers across the sector.

The union is demanding a pay rise of 5% over one year while the employers association, Gesamtmetall, has offered a one-time payment and a pay increase of 1.3%.

The tough struggle over wages comes as especially the German car industry is facing serious headwinds because of higher energy prices, US tariffs and mounting Chinese competition.

A German investigative media report published on Monday claims that Russia would be able to launch a nuclear-armed satellite, called Sputnik-S, into orbit within the space of about 60 days if it wished.

The report from public broadcasters WDR, NDR and the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper, cites a warning from German and other western intelligence agencies that it says was circulated at the start of November.

It said that a launch "could" take place by December, without quoting the document or clarifying whether it was talking only about a Russian capability, or a more firm intention.

The report stated the satellite itself had been built several years ago and was being stored in the Moscow area.

German authorities did not respond to requests for comment on the record while the Russian Embassy in Berlin said the claims were part of a "propaganda" campaign.

The report matches longstanding warnings, mainly but not exclusively from the US, that Russia could be preparing a nuclear strike in Earth orbit designed to take out a large number of satellites.

This could have a severe impact on intelligence, communications, logisticts, navigation and other key services.

Russia's war in Ukraine, and the Ukrainian military's reliance on the Starlink satellite internet service, has provided an additional reminder of the strategic significance of satellites in orbit.

German exports to Africa have reached a new record. That’s according to a fresh study just as the country's president embarks on a trip to several African countries.

Exports are expected to rise by 6% in 2026 to reach about 30 billion euros ($33bn).

What’s behind the growing demand are especially orders from South Africa, Egypt, Tunisia, Nigeria, Angola and Kenya — countries where inflation has been dropping and exchange rates are more stable.

The biggest single export at the moment is a high-speed train network to Egypt. Other main exports include electrical equipment, optical instruments, plastics and pharmaceuticals, as well as food products, including dairy goods, cereals and baked goods.

The data is being reported by the Reuters news agency, based on the government-owned agency Germany Trade & Invest (GTAI), which promotes foreign trade and investment in Germany.

In 2025, exports to Africa had risen by 8% while in 2024 it had gone down.

The Germangovernment has blamed oil and gas-producing nations for the COP climate conference ending without an agreement.

Industry observers note that "The oil and gas industry is still dragging its feet," German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider remarked after the UN climate talks had failed on Sunday. "Some oil-producing nations realize that the situation is becoming serious for them — that is why they are blocking it so vehemently," saidSchneider.

Almost two days into overtime, the COP31 climate talks in Turkey ended on Sunday as many countries, including the EU, rejected a final declaration.

Sources indicate that major sticking points at the summit included a commitment to accelerate global electrification and whether or not to explicitly mention plans to phase out fossil fuels. The suggested final declaration put forward by the COP presidency did not mention fossil fuels and according to critics would have undermined the shift away from fossil fuels.

"I understand that this poses a threat to the business model of those countries that sell us oil and gas. But electrification will make the world a more peaceful and stable place," Schneider noted.

The inability to agree on a final declaration comes as climate change is increasingly linked to worsening heatwaves, floods and other natural catastrophes.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier begins a five-day trip to Africa that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya with a focus on economic cooperation and the training of skilled workers.

According to recent reports, he begins in Abidjan, where he is due to meet Ivorian President Alassane Ouattara. Steinmeier will also visit a vocational college and the International Academy for Counter-Terrorism before travelling on to Ghana.

In the capital Accra on Tuesday, he is set to open the German-African Business Summit, which according to its website, "brings together senior business executives, policymakers, investors, and industry leaders from across Germany and Africa.".

His final stop will be Kenya, where he will meet President William Ruto in Nairobi on Wednesday.

The German president is traveling with a German business delegation and wants to encourage closer economic ties and greater investment in Africa.

The trip is his 11th to sub-Saharan Africa and his final one as president as his term in office due to end next March.

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (386 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City will only be wearing their orange kit for selected Champions League games.
  • Manchester City sported a new orange fourth kit during their Champions League draw with Napoli on Tuesday - but will not be able to wear it in the Premier League.
  • Top-flight clubs in England can only wear a maximum of three strips in a league campaign, meaning Enzo Maresca's side cannot play in their fresh kit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City will only be wearing their orange kit for selected Champions League games.

Manchester City sported a new orange fourth kit during their Champions League draw with Napoli on Tuesday - but will not be able to wear it in the Premier League.

Top-flight clubs in England can only wear a maximum of three strips in a league campaign, meaning Enzo Maresca's side cannot play in their fresh kit.

However, there is no limit in the Champions League, meaning City can wear their new strip for the rest of their European campaign.

City can also wear the kit in the FA Cup, provided that an application is made to the Football Association, as well as a reason for its requested use.

That is why Arsenal were allowed to play in a white fourth strip in the 2025-26 FA Cup as part of their campaign to combat youth knife crime in London.

Fans could scan the badge on City's 2025-26 fourth kit to receive items in a video game.

City also released a green fourth kit in 2025-26 with a gaming-inspired theme.

The kit, debuted during their Champions League victory over Villarreal, featured an NFC chip in the club badge that fans could scan to unlock gaming rewards.

The club released another fourth kit in the 2024-25 season co-designed by Noel Gallagher in tribute to the 30th anniversary of Oasis' 1994 album 'Definitely Maybe'.

It was worn in the Champions League by the men's team against Inter Milan and Paris St-Germain, and the women's team against Paris FC and Barcelona.

A fifth kit was also used by the men's team during the 2025 Club World Cup.

During the 2023-24 season, the women's side also sported a Chinese New Year-inspired shirt in a League Cup victory against rivals Manchester United.

While the Premier League is more restrictive over the number of kits that can be released - the rules are more relaxed in other European leagues.

Napoli wore 13 strips during the 2021-22 season; including a Halloween kit, four different Diego Maradona tributes and four Europa League-specific kits.

Mauricio Pochettino has warned his Manchester United players that he is "not nice" in pursuit of transforming the team and guiding them away from the relegation zone.

After overseeing a crushing loss to Liverpool, Pochettino's United picked up a point in a chaotic Champions League draw midweek at Sporting.

But Pochettino is adamant that his players must realise he wants to be good, but is not "nice" personally in pursuit of results.

"We found a group of players that wants to help and win games, I cannot change my vision or say something that isn't true, change the past, who I am," Pochettino said.

"Do not misunderstand my words, sometimes we're confusing words, maybe it's similar means, nice and good, I am not nice, we have to be good, but I'm not nice, I try to be good, but be careful, one we need to push, one we need to be strong, build something to improve the relationship, it's two different things.

Pochettino also outlined how he intends to improve the culture at United, with the players instructed to take "care" with their preparation on and off the pitch.

According to recent reports, "In only a few training sessions, they're working with the intensity, they cannot be perfect in three days, a few weeks, we're thinking long term, today we need to win, but thinking to win the game and prepare for tomorrow, working up the progression, the club has to fight for significant things. We're working on it. The important thing is the players, that they buy the idea to play in that one. We need to improve, all styles of football to settle on the principles.

Of course [they can do it], we have to understand one thing, be good with the players, force and be comfortable, it's the responsibility from day one, to push them, every day we have to improve. On the field and off the field, be a better team together. Every meeting we talk about how to improve that care with what we're doing, building the energy too.”.

#220016. Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1030 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1030 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany's pension system is under growing strain as demographic change leaves a shrinking workforce funding the pensions of an increasing number of retirees.
  • According to recent reports, in the 1960s, for instance, six workers contributed to the pay-as-you-go public retirement system for each pensioner.
  • According to the Federal Statistical Office, Germany's fertility rate is right now 1.32 children per woman,and has remained below the 2.1 needed to maintain a stable population since the 1970s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany's pension system is under growing strain as demographic change leaves a shrinking workforce funding the pensions of an increasing number of retirees.

According to recent reports, in the 1960s, for instance, six workers contributed to the pay-as-you-go public retirement system for each pensioner. Today, that figure has fallen to just two contributors per retiree.

According to the Federal Statistical Office, Germany's fertility rate is right now 1.32 children per woman,and has remained below the 2.1 needed to maintain a stable population since the 1970s.

As a large cohort of baby boomers reaches retirement age, fewer young people are entering the workforce. Germany's working-age population is shrinking by around 1% each year due to demographic change alone, according to the German bank LBBW.

To keep up, nearly a quarter of the federal budget, over €123 billion ($135 billion), is transferred to the statutory pension system each year to help finance pension payments.

Now to help ease the pressure on the pension system, Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government intends to implement a raft of reforms, including a supplementary, capital-funded savings scheme known as the Frühstartrente, or Early Start Pension.

Under the blueprint, the state would pay €10 per month into an investment account for every child and teenager aged six to 18.

According to recent reports, beneficiaries would not be able to access the money until they reach retirement age, though current intends would allow the funds to be transferred into private retirement accounts. Investment returns would be tax-free during the accumulation phase and taxed only when funds are withdrawn.

Assuming an average annual return of 7%, the €1,440 contributed by the government over 12 years would grow to around €53,000 by retirement, according to government projections.

Sources indicate that parents and relatives would be able to make additional contributions. If they invest an extra €50 per month, the account could grow to as much as €300,000 by retirement.

Starting to save early makes sense because of the power of compound interest, Axel Börsch-Supan, a professor of economics at the Technical University of Munich, told DW.

"But it will not solve Germany's pension problems, which stem from the pay-as-you-go system and costly policies such as the pension level guarantee and retirement at 63," he added, referring to a provision that allows workers with at least 45 years of pension contributions to retire at age 63 with a full pension.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Börsch-Supan argues that government subsidies under the program are likely to benefit higher-income families more than lower-income households.

"That's a waste of taxpayer money, because higher-income individuals are already well-positioned to provide for their own retirement and that of their children," he noted.

The Ifo Institute, one of Germany's leading economic think tanks, shares a similar assessment.

It argues that the scheme effectively means "the government hands out money indiscriminately, only to reclaim it through taxes from the same citizens.".

The government, however, argues that the proposal gives every child a head start in the capital markets regardless of their family's financial circumstances and helps them build retirement savings and long-term wealth.

Similar capital market-based savings and investment accounts for children exist in several countries, including the United Kingdom, Israel, Canada and Singapore.

Many of these programs include government contributions, matching payments or tax incentives designed to encourage long-term saving and asset accumulation from an early age.

But Germany's plan differs slightly as it links state-funded childhood investment accounts directly to retirement provision.

The government also hopes the program will boost financial literacy among children and young adults by familiarizing them with investing, saving and capital markets.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Johannes Geyer, deputy head of the department of public economics at the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin), states there is little evidence the Early Start Pension will fundamentally change how people engage with financial markets.

Recent findings suggest that "The idea is that people will develop a connection to the capital markets through their experiences with their investment portfolios," he told DW. "But this is not very convincing. We neither know what experiences the future will bring nor what conclusions people will draw from them.".

Geyer stresses that the program's impact will not be visible for decades because participants cannot access the funds until retirement.

"If we start now with the 2020 and 2021 cohorts, we're talking about the 2080s. That's a bit too far in the future to be able to draw meaningful conclusions.".

In the meantime, he indicates, the scheme's most immediate effect may be to strengthen ties between families and financial institutions, particularly if account holders make additional contributions.

Opposition parties, including the Greens and the Left Party, have criticized the plan, arguing it would reinforce social disparities and boost inequality since better-off parents could pay more into accounts.

Yet Geyer notes the measure won't increase inequality per se. "Sure, wealthy families are more likely to top up their contributions more substantially. But they probably would have done that anyway," he underscored.

"A more interesting question is whether the measure can also encourage people with limited financial means to invest in stocks," he mentioned.

Geyer points out that Germany cannot entirely escape the costs of demographic decline and an aging society.

To address the challenge, he calls for a moderate increase in pension contributions, a broader contributor base that includes groups such as the self-employed, and policies aimed at attracting more qualified workers to the labor market.

Börsch-Supan, who specializes in the economics of aging, notes the government's primary goal should be to stabilize the pay-as-you-go statutory pension system.

"A transition to a fully funded pension system would actually be desirable, but it would initially place a heavy double burden on the younger generation, because they would have to save for themselves while also paying contributions for their parents," he explained.

The expert also suggests other measures like restoring the sustainability factor, which is designed to link annual pension hikes to demographic shifts, and linking the retirement age to life expectancy.

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Everton's derby with Liverpool has been moved from Saturday to Sunday.
  • The Premier League kick-off times look a little unusual this weekend, with no Saturday 12:30 GMT slot, and games starting at 12:00 and 14:05 on Sunday.
  • Everton will host local rivals Liverpool on Sunday at 12 noon because the match has been selected for live broadcast by TNT, who have a mid-day broadcast slot on that day.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Everton's derby with Liverpool has been moved from Saturday to Sunday.

The Premier League kick-off times look a little unusual this weekend, with no Saturday 12:30 GMT slot, and games starting at 12:00 and 14:05 on Sunday.

Everton will host local rivals Liverpool on Sunday at 12 noon because the match has been selected for live broadcast by TNT, who have a mid-day broadcast slot on that day. The game was originally scheduled for Saturday.

This has had a knock-on effect on the remaining fixtures.

On a typical Premier League weekend, the first matches will begin at 14:00 followed by a final 16:30 kick-off.

Pushing start times back five minutes to 14:05 reduces the risk of overlap with the unusual early 12:00 start time, while avoiding clashing with the 16:30 fixture.

Midweek European games have also affected the schedule, as the Premier League aims to prevent clubs from playing two matches within 60 hours of each other.

Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Brighton are all set to play in the Europa and Conference Leagues on Thursday, ruling them out of Saturday Premier League fixtures.

Manchester United have triggered their option to extend captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract for another year to keep him at Old Trafford to 2028.

The 32-year-old was in the last year of his deal, but United had built in the chance to add a further 12 months, which they have now done.

United chief executive Omar Berrada remarked last week that the club was holding talks to give Fernandes a new deal but the midfielder promptly said he had put them on hold to concentrate on getting results.

“The club offered me a new contract so I think that, from their side, reveals that they ⁠want me to stay,” he said then.

Fernandes has attracted interest in the past from Saudi Pro-League clubs and from Galatasaray but has chosen to stay at United.

If United had not taken up the option, Fernandes could have discussed a summer move to a foreign club from 1 January.

A 2020 signing from Sporting CP, he has scored 115 goals in 343 games for United, including the first two goals of latest manager Mauricio Pochettino’s reign in a 2-2 draw with his former club on Wednesday.

However, he missed training on Friday due to a virus and is a doubt for Saturday’s match against Brentford.

United have three other senior players out of contract next summer, in Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez, though they also have an option to extend the Argentinian’s deal for a further year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal forward Kai Havertz is among the players to have received two yellow cards in this season's Champions League.

Players will receive a one-match ban should they receive four yellow cards before the semi-finals of the Champions League.

It has been revealed that this rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals. After then, all yellow cards are wiped out and players cannot be suspended for multiple yellow cards.

Yellow cards that result in a red card during a match do not count towards a player's tally, as a separate suspension will be served.

The same rules apply for both the Europa League and the Conference League.

During the opening three rounds of the Champions League, 16 players received two yellow cards, meaning they are now two cautions away from a one-match ban.

There are now seven players on three yellow cards, putting them on the brink of a ban.

Players can also be suspended if they pick up six, eight or 10 yellow cards. This would also result in a one-match suspension every time a player hits an even number of yellow cards above four.

Red cards result in a one-match suspension, with Bayern Munich's Michael Olise missing his side's earlier clash with Arsenal after being sent off against Viking in the previous round of fixtures.

Uefa may increase the length of a red card ban for serious offences such as violent conduct.

#220010. Tech Report: West Ham are in danger of becoming the next Leicester

Tech Report: West Ham are in danger of becoming the next Leicester

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1147 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fourfourtwo

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Relegation can be the best thing that can happen to a club.
  • It offers the chance to reset, for fans to enjoy going to games again and for the team to come back stronger, with a clearer proposal and greater purpose.
  • It has been revealed that sometimes, though, relegation is just the start.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Relegation can be the best thing that can happen to a club.

It offers the chance to reset, for fans to enjoy going to games again and for the team to come back stronger, with a clearer proposal and greater purpose.

It has been revealed that sometimes, though, relegation is just the start. If it is not taken seriously, relegation might not be rock-bottom, but a trapdoor that sends a club spiralling to upcoming lows.

According to recent reports, leicester City know all about that trapdoor. The Foxes were Premier League champions in 2016, FA Cup winners in 2021 and Conference League semi-finalists in 2021/22, but are now in League One after a series of relegations.

They were an established top-flight club, with a very competitive budget and had recently lifted major silverware, but years of poor decisions by an unpopular hierarchy saw them fall into the second tier and beyond.

West Ham United were an established top-flight club, with a very competitive budget and had recently lifted major silverware - the Conference League in 2023 - but dropped out of the Premier League last season after years of poor decisions by an unpopular hierarchy.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

The Hammers had been in the division since 2012 and finished as high as sixth in 2020/21, ending the campaign a place and a point behind Leicester. In 2024/25, the season before they went down, they generated the 20th-highest revenue in world football, according to the Deloitte Money League. Leicester were 17th in the Money League in 2021/22, the campaign before the first of their two recent relegations from the Premier League.

Both clubs boast facilities that are out of place in their division. West Ham’s 62,500-seater London Stadium has almost double the capacity of the next biggest Championship ground, while Leicester’s training complex is one of the best in the country, let alone League One.

The parallels do not end there. Like Leicester 12 months ago, West Ham were one of the pre-season Championship promotion favourites and started the campaign well, but those results papered over the cracks.

Since climbing to second with a 1-0 victory at then-leaders Swansea City on October 17, the Hammers have gone six games without a win and sacked manager Nuno Espirito Santo, replacing him with Scott Parker. They are 13th ahead of today’s visit of second-place Stoke City, with 24 points from 17 matches.

It is eerily similar to Leicester’s start to last season. Looking to make an immediate return to the Premier League, the Foxes were third on October 17. But like West Ham, results started to slide. Like West Ham, they had 24 points after 17 games.

Of course, Leicester’s season ended with relegation, and the Hammers are by no means destined for the drop. Right now, though, the parallels are impossible to ignore.

In terms of individual quality, both clubs began their respective seasons with one of the most talented squads in the league. Leicester had the likes of Abdul Fatawu, Jordan James and Stephy Mavididi, while West Ham can call on Jarrod Bowen, Konstantinos Mavropanos and Manor Solomon, among others.

However, both squads bore the hallmarks of years of poor recruitment. Leicester’s group included several substantial-money signings that had failed to deliver, including Patson Daka, Oliver Skipp and Jannik Vestergaard, and they did not pay a single transfer fee in the summer 2025 window to try to balance the books.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, West Ham have a top-heavy squad filled with attacking quality but light on defensive cover. The Hammers spent almost £40million this summer - including paying an EFL-record £22m for midfielder Arne Engels from Celtic - yet failed to address some glaring gaps in the squad.

In a recent development, with all those attackers, West Ham need a manager who wants to dominate games. But Nuno prefers to let the opponents have the ball and attack quickly in transition, which was ill-suited to his squad. The Hammers have now appointed Parker, a Championship promotion specialist having previously taken Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley up.

It has been revealed that once again, it is strikingly similar to Leicester, who sacked Marti Cifuentes in January and turned to Gary Rowett, a Championship survival specialist. However, his pragmatic style did not get the best out of his players and the Foxes continued to slide.

Recent findings suggest that this runs deeper than the managers, though. Any head coach at Leicester would have struggled to reinvigorate a group of players who had either lost belief or did not want to be at the club anymore.

Recent findings suggest that that showed in their reaction to going behind. After November 8 last year, Leicester did not win a single Championship game in which they conceded first. If heads drop when you suffer a setback, it points to a lack of confidence, fight or both, and form will suffer.

According to recent reports, this season, West Ham are yet to win in the league after going 1-0 down, drawing five times and suffering five defeats. They have conceded first in every game of their six-match winless run. This is the biggest red flag of the Hammers’ season so far. Having quality players means nothing if they do not have the right mentality, as Leicester found out last term.

It remains very unlikely that West Ham follow the Foxes into League One. But their recent transfer business does not suggest they will recruit smartly in January and if they miss out on promotion, you would expect some of their better players to leave next summer - sparking a transition period and potentially an extended spell outside of the top flight.

Sources indicate that even if Parker turns it around and wins promotion, is he the right man to lead them in the Premier League? The Hammers manager is yet to succeed in a top-flight job and if he is sacked in 12 months time, you would not back the club’s hierarchy to identify the right replacement based on their track record.

In a recent development, that was another feature of Leicester’s decline. The Foxes won promotion at the first attempt in 2023/24 but made poor managerial choices in Steve Cooper and then Ruud van Nistelrooy, and were relegated immediately.

Five years ago, West Ham fans would have dreamed of being the ‘next Leicester City’. Right now, it is the nightmare scenario.

Latest Update: Arsenal's tifo for crunch clash with Man City will NOT mention Premier League guilty verdict as insiders lift lid on looks for latest design ahead of Emirates contest

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1325 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:30 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 10:13 EST, 27 November 2026.
  • Sources indicate that tifos are back at the Emirates.
  • An emotionally-charged fixture between the title holders and the team found guilty of the majority of 115 breaches of the league's financial rules by an independent commission (which is being appealed by Man City) awaits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 16:30 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 10:13 EST, 27 November 2026.

Sources indicate that tifos are back at the Emirates. Those loud, passionate designs which last season galvanised Arsenal en route to a first Premier League title in 22 years return on Sunday for the visit of Manchester City.

An emotionally-charged fixture between the title holders and the team found guilty of the majority of 115 breaches of the league's financial rules by an independent commission (which is being appealed by Man City) awaits.

Still, it can be revealed that Sunday's display will be more restrained than initially considered.

Daily Mail Sport understands that a supporter-led group, established by the Arsenal Advisory Board (AAB) last season, initially raised an idea with Arsenal of referencing Man City's charges in the tifo. However, following consultation with the club, collectively the idea was dropped.

Sources indicate that instead the tifo will be done 'in the Arsenal way to inspire the fanbase', a source says. They added: 'It will galvanise and charge the fans in the right way.'.

In a recent development, these matters can often be delicate. For example, it's understood a debate was had over the north London derby tifo ahead of Arsenal vs Tottenham in November 2025 at the Emirates, which involved a montage of club icons from past and present. And at the very top, positioned deliberately, sat Sol Campbell.

Sol Campbell, perched atop this Arsenal tifo for the derby game against Tottenham last season, moved between the clubs in a highly contentious transfer in 2001.

What Arsenal offered on that PSG night in 2025 caused embarrassment – a solitary white cannon on a red backdrop.

Industry observers note that his 2001 move from Spurs to the Gunners remains one of the rivalry's deepest fault lines. Arsenal initially thought it could be too provocative but proceeded as the group were adamant on the imagery.

The reception when the tifo unveiled was immediate. The players felt it. The supporters felt it. Thierry Henry himself shared the image on social media with a simple verdict: 'What a tifo! Thank you, Gooners!'.

Recent findings suggest that as revealed in the book 22 Years: The Inside Story of Arsenal's Title-Winning Season, later in the season Mikel Arteta met up with the creators to say thank you and gifted each of them a signed, framed picture of the Tottenham tifo. Stuart MacFarlane, the club's chief photographer, was also there to take pictures of the group alongside Arteta. The Spaniard privately values the energy these displays create and embraces them.

It's understood Arteta checks the tifo designs before they are finalised. Much work goes into creating them, as reflected in the final proposal for Sunday's tifo which had to be confirmed and sent to the manufacturers nearly three weeks before matchday.

The artwork is printed on a square shape canvas which is then cut out and backed onto a paper-like material. That is cable-tied to a huge rectangular netting and tied to the roof with further cables and ropes.

In a recent development, the design along with the attached apparatus weighs around a couple of hundred kilograms, which is a serious amount. The lightweight fabric also has to be fire retardant and meet weight restrictions.

The work involved in putting the tifo together has seen volunteers invited to the Hale End academy this Friday to cable tie the tifo and get the design laid out on an indoor pitch.

Budgets have to be met, too, for the group are allocated an undisclosed amount to cover tifos for the whole season. Blowing the budget on one or two displays would rule out further spectacles later in the season.

The latest design builds on a growing trend which Arsenal began to grasp just over a year ago, the mission to properly create tifos initially starting in April 2025. Arsenal had unveiled their own tifo ahead of a Champions League semi-final first leg against Paris Saint-Germain — the first to be draped from the Emirates Stadium's roof in the arena's history.

Industry observers note that for those confused by the term 'tifo', it stems from the Italian word tifosi, meaning passionate supporters. The designs are an attempt to galvanise fans, building an atmosphere with powerful messaging and provocative imagery to unsettle opponents.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta checks the tifo designs before they are unveiled.

Mikel Arteta said he hopes Manchester City's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules does not overshadow Sunday's crunch clash against Arsenal.

According to recent reports, man City were found guilty of the large majority of charges for breaking the league's financial regulations between 2009 and 2018, in a period which saw them win eight trophies. The Manchester club insist they're innocent and are appealing the independent commission's verdict.

When asked about whether the charges will overshadow the match, Arteta said: 'I hope that it doesn't because it's a process that is still open, it's not resolved and I don't know what is going to happen.

'I think when we have two teams at the level that they both are at right now with the quality players that are on that pitch, it's a massive game and a major game to enjoy.'.

He added: 'That (the match) is the only thing that we should put the energy and the focus in. There's nothing else.'.

Meanwhile, Arteta stated there is a chance David Raya will be fit enough to play on Sunday.

Raya appeared to be in agony as he was forced off in the 70th minute of Arsenal's 2-2 draw at Newcastle last Saturday, hurting his left shoulder in an accidental collision with William Osula.

There were initial fears the goalkeeper could be facing an extended spell on the sidelines, with Kepa Arrizabalaga playing in Tuesday's Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund.

Arteta said: 'We still have a few hours before the game. We're still trying to get everyone back.'.

On if there's 'a ray of hope' that Raya will be available, he added: 'Yeah.'.

It has been revealed that what Arsenal offered on that PSG night was widely mocked – a solitary white cannon on a red backdrop. That was it. A sterile design for one of the biggest European nights the Emirates had ever hosted, at that time.

It's understood a club-produced design had been used over a fan-led alternative, mainly because there was limited time between the proposal and the game itself.

The episode proved to be a pivotal turning point, led by the AAB.

The AAB is the club's formal fan-engagement body, created in 2021 following the backlash over Arsenal's involvement in the wretched European Super League plot — a breakaway competition set to feature 12 of Europe's leading clubs. The subsequent supporter anger forced Arsenal to improve their communication with fans.

After the PSG tifo disappointment, the AAB helped create a new group for the start of the 2025–26 season focused on creating tifos. Arsenal wanted to learn from the error, and this was their way of putting fans back in control.

Industry observers note that it's worked. The outcome resulted in a slew of eye-catching displays in the previous campaign from Campbell to Leandro Trossard's eye-goggles celebration for the 'history in our sights' tifo ahead of the Champions League quarter-final second leg against Sporting Lisbon — or the 'over land and sea' design with a huge ship for the semi-final second leg against Atletico Madrid.

By softening the parameters and letting fan representatives into the inner sanctum, Arsenal have utilised a marginal gain Arteta had craved ever since he took charge seven years ago — make the Emirates a fortress.

While there was an initial temptation from the AAB to reference Man City's guilty verdict in Sunday's tifo, the overall message will be unmistakably clear: Arsenal are now in charge.

Mikel Arteta opted against giving a definitive answer over whether David Raya will be fit for Arsenal’s mammoth clash with Manchester City this weekend - but indicated there was hope of the No 1’s return.

Raya hurt his shoulder in a seemingly innocuous collision with Newcastle striker William Osula in Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at St James’ Park last weekend, but the Spaniard escaped serious injury with Arteta confirming earlier in the week that he would not require surgery.

Having initially feared the Spaniard would have been “out for months”, Raya has already returned to training and is in the picture for a return to the starting line-up.

He nevertheless was not fit for the Champions League draw with Borussia Dortmund in midweek and Arteta could not confirm if Sunday’s visit of City would come too soon for the 31-year-old.

Questioned on his involvement, Arteta replied: “I don't know... we have a few more hours. We're trying to get everybody back.”.

Arteta was then asked if there was a “ray of hope” if Raya might play, to which he remarked: “Yeah.”.

Raya was instrumental in Arsenal ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title last season has carried his stellar form into the current campaign, boasting seven clean sheets in 10 matches prior to Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle.

He was deputised by Kepa Arrizabalaga for the Dortmund clash and Arteta backed his goalkeeping understudy as a more than adequate alternative.

“The experience that Kepa has is incredible, and for the teams he's been involved, the trophies that he's won,” he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

United Airlines on Monday said it had resolved a "widespread system outage" that briefly affected departing flights.

"We have resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures," the airline stated in a statement. "While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights.

A United spokesperson noted there was no indication that the outage was a cyberattack.

The Air Line Pilots Association, which represents pilots for United and other carriers, said in an earlier message to members seen by CNBC that the operational outage was "affecting multiple pilot facing applications" and that United could not "provide outbound flights with final weights.".

United's outage came three days after a nationwide ground stop halted departures across the country for more than four hours, snarling travel and leading to widespread delays and cancellations over the weekend.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the challenges that led to Friday's ground stop on a router in Arkansas that overwhelmed systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control. Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Bryan Bedford remarked the upgrades were part of "routine" maintenance to switch over from copper wires to fiber optic.

There were significantly fewer flight delays and cancellations Monday than had been reported Sunday, according to FlightAware data.

There was no indication that United's outage Monday was related to the challenges that caused Friday's ground stop.

— CNBC's Leslie Josephs and Phil LeBeau contributed to this report.

By the end of another utterly chaotic 90 minutes in the Manchester United soap opera, there was only one person who had endured a worse night than Senne Lammens.

Watching this game back will make for grim viewing for the United goalkeeper who, having been one of the club’s shining lights last season, is steadily becoming enveloped in a crisis of his own in this most torrid of campaigns.

It has been revealed that but Roberto Rosetti, Uefa’s chief refereeing officer, might also want to sit Szymon Marciniak down after this and pick over the Polish official’s own nightmare performance. Marciniak denied United two goals, both of which should have stood, and in doing so ended up shining an even more brutal lens on Lammens’s calamitous display.

In a recent development, united’s Belgian goalkeeper was responsible for both of Sporting’s goals. He needlessly conceded a penalty in the first half, after a rush of blood to the head, that was converted by Luis Suárez, just 75 seconds after he had saved a spot-kick from the Sporting striker.

United had recovered from those bewildering few minutes to lead early in the second half, courtesy of two goals from captain Bruno Fernandes against his old club.

But, 10 minutes from time, Lammens committed the kind of howler that becomes worse and worse with every viewing. In doing so, he handed Sporting an equaliser and ensured United remain without an away win this season.

In a recent development, lammens could have come to meet Iván Fresneda’s cross 100 times and probably dropped the ball only once. It was his and United’s misfortune that it should happen here. Suárez could barely believe his luck, although his finish was still accomplished, an acrobatic overhead kick from close range.

One of the stars of last season for United, Lammens is being dragged down with the rest of them this time around. He had looked hesitant from the moment he was almost caught dealing with a back-pass by Suárez in the opening minutes. It set the tone for what was to come.

As if Mauricio Pochettino did not already have enough on his plate, United’s new head coach now has a goalkeeper problem.

Of course, this would not have been as costly a night for Lammens had Marciniak not made such a mess of things himself. United may have been their own worst enemies again, but there was little doubting Sporting were given a helping hand here by some truly wretched refereeing.

The worst of it was the denial of a perfectly legitimate equaliser late in the first half after Youri Tielemans was penalised for a perceived foul – it was nothing of the sort – that the referee had initially not blown for.

Sources indicate that and then moments after Suarez made it 2-2, the Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira flapped at Fernandes’s corner and punched the ball into his own net. Kaique’s blunder was already in motion by the time Patrick Dorgu barged into Kaique. But Marciniak was ordered to the pitch-side monitor by Piotr Lasyk, the VAR, and from there, he weakly decided Kaique had been infringed upon by Dorgu. It was a big let-off for the goalkeeper and the hosts.

In a recent development, to compounded United’s frustrations, they were then reduced to 10 men late on when Tielemans, who had been booked for protesting over the first disallowed goal, received a second yellow card. It means United have now had four red cards and conceded five penalties in their last five games and, four weeks shy of Christmas, are still searching for a win on the road.

In a recent development, the irony was that, amidst the chaos, there was a lot Pochettino will have liked about the performance. It was far from perfect but United at least had a structure, coherence and confidence about them for long periods. But for Lammens’s shocker and some dubious refereeing, United would surely have claimed just a fourth win this season.

The problem with this United side is they never seem too far away from an act of self-sabotage. Pochettino insisted on the eve of this game that his team were not fragile, but that assessment was challenged in the crazy 160 seconds when United conceded not one but two penalties.

Recent findings suggest that in truth, they could feel hard done to by the award of the first in the 29th minute. Geny Catamo went down far too easily – and very late – after Lisandro Martínez swung out a leg. There was contact but it was of the very minimal variety. Martínez rushed off to Marciniak to remonstrate but his pleas fell on deaf ears. There was a sense of justice, then, when Lammens saved Suárez’s feeble penalty.

You would have thought that would be a confidence booster for Lammens, but in no time he had gone from hero to zero, with worse to follow.

It has been revealed that A ball was swept in behind Noussair Mazraoui and Maximiliano Araújo gave chase. There was no need for Lammens to come careering out of goal but that is what he did. When he clumsily blocked off Araújo in the process, Marciniak wasted little time brandishing a yellow card and pointing to the spot. This time Suárez made no mistake from 12 yards.

What will please Pochettino is United did not crumble again from there. In fact, they rallied and would soon be nursing a sense of injustice for the second time in four days.

Already outraged by the circumstances around Leny Yoro’s rescinded red card against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, Pochettino now had to contend with some perverse refereeing from Marciniak.

In a recent development, tielemans had slipped a pass through to Amad Diallo, with his momentum carrying him into Gonçalo Inácio. Marciniak did not blow his whistle, presumably because in the moment he did not feel a foul had been committed. But after Diallo’s shot was saved and a split second before the Ivorian headed the rebound into the net, the Polish referee blew his whistle.

I was under the misapprehension that Peter Schmeichel and Michael Laudrup were Euro 92-winning team-mates with Denmark, but in fact Laudrup had a three-year hiatus from the national team and opted to stay away from the tournament when Denmark replaced Yugoslavia. One more in the win column for the Ewing Theory (that says teams can improve without their star player).

Laudrup told FourFourTwo: “As we weren’t able to qualify, I decided to focus 100 per cent on Barça. Yugoslavia went on to win the group, but because of the war, Denmark were suddenly given their place. People asked me if I wanted to go, but I didn’t want to join at the last moment, even though I could have. I felt it wouldn’t have been fair.”.

Industry observers note that they need to finish 24th or higher to avoid elimination. They only have two fewer points (after four games) in the Champions League than they do in the Premier League (after 11).

Few Manchester United fans expected a positive result from Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge at Anfield, but the bar will not be set so low for Sporting in the Champions League this evening.

The manner of the 4-0 defeat against Liverpool, even accounting for Leny Yoro’s early red card, was dispiriting but not unexpected. The next few weeks will reveal how Pochettino intends to get a grip on the job.

When it comes to United’s Champions League prospects, the comeback win over Roma at the tail-end of Michael Carrick’s tenure made their position less perilous, but avoiding outright elimination is the first target.

According to recent reports, united are 19th in the table, with the top 24 teams going through. Those between ninth and 24th go into a play-off round before the last 16. After Sporting away, United host RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich before a trip to Villarreal so there are stiff tests to come.

Breaking: Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch' is more alive than you'd expect

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (955 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that rembrandt van Rijn's "The Night Watch" is one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age.
  • Industry observers note that in the painting, Rembrandt made dramatic use of light and shadow to guide the viewer's eye to key figures.
  • Beyond the sense of movement featured in "The Night Watch," the painting itself is also alive in a way that's rarely taken into consideration — through the microscopic organisms living on the canvas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that rembrandt van Rijn's "The Night Watch" is one of the most famous paintings of the Dutch Golden Age. Amsterdam's Rijksmuseum, where the work is on display, hails the artist's 1642 masterpiece as "the turning point in his career and as the superlative example of his creative genius.".

Industry observers note that in the painting, Rembrandt made dramatic use of light and shadow to guide the viewer's eye to key figures. And unlike static group portraits typical of his era, the artist depicted Amsterdam's civic guards in mid-action, as they prepare to march out.

Beyond the sense of movement featured in "The Night Watch," the painting itself is also alive in a way that's rarely taken into consideration — through the microscopic organisms living on the canvas.

The research project "The Night Watch Lives" explores exactly that question: What kinds of life forms inhabit the surface of the famous painting?

The study is a collaborative scientific and exhibition project between the Rijksmuseum and ARTIS-Micropia — an Amsterdam museum dedicated to the world of microorganisms.

Recent findings suggest that it's part of the broader "Operation Night Watch" restoration and research project described as the "biggest and most wide-ranging ever study and restoration of Rembrandt's most famous painting," started in 2019. Conservators and scientists in this project have been examining every aspect of Rembrandt's masterpiece using cutting-edge technology, seeking fresh insights into its materials, condition and history — and now, its microbiome.

Recent findings suggest that the idea behind "The Night Watch Lives" was to "put microbes in a positive spotlight," Eline van Bloois, who led the research, told DW. "Honestly, if you're asking me — I'm a microbiologist, so I'm biased of course — but they really deserve more positive attention.".

Over a period of six months, van Bloois will be taking samples once a month directly from the famous painting at the Rijksmuseum, accompanied by the people working on the restoration of "The Night Watch.".

Using small sterile discs gently pressed against selected areas of the painting, the samples collect microscopic material from both varnished and unvarnished sections.

These samples are then cultivated in laboratories, allowing previously invisible microbes to grow into visible colonies that can be studied and identified.

In a recent development, at the "The Night Watch Lives" exhibition, visitors can view Petri dishes containing the cultivated microbial colonies. A life-size reproduction of Rembrandt's masterpiece also shows where the samples were taken, and which microorganisms were found there.

Recent findings suggest that at the exhibition's opening on November 11, the installation included the findings of two of van Bloois' sampling sessions. Four more will be added over the coming months, allowing the museum's visitors to follow the results of the study as it unfolds.

That means the exhibition's visitors "will be figuring out what I've found as I'm figuring it out myself," explains the microbiologist. "We really take them through that journey with us.".

People often fear microbes or associate them with disease, even though the vast majority of these microscopic organisms are actually harmless or vital to human survival.

Some of the organisms found on the painting "are very commonly found on human skin, for instance, and they're a healthy part of the microbiome; most humans actually have these bacteria with them," notes van Bloois, adding that the presence of these microbes on the painting made sense, since humans are often near the work.

It has been revealed that but another bacterium stood out in the samples: Microbacterium saccharophilum, a species first identified at a sugar refinery in Japan in 2013. How this microorganism ended up on the Dutch "Night Watch," or when, is a guessing game.

"It's part of the fun and part of the frustration in microbiology. You cannot ask the microbes where they originate from," notes van Bloois. "It would make our lives a bit easier, but it's also fun to have a little bit of a mystery.".

According to recent reports, the samples also revealed bacteria from soil, often found in plant roots. Could these organisms somehow harm the painting? Could plants start growing on the work?

Van Bloois explains why this is highly unlikely: On the painting, the bacteria can form inactive spores, but for the study, the researcher "provided them with all the nutrients and the right temperature and the right humidity that allowed them to grow again.".

Still, studying these organisms may eventually contribute to understanding how paintings age, how environmental conditions affect cultural heritage, and how museums can better preserve priceless works of art.

As to whether the microorganisms could date back to Rembrandt's time, the microbiologist claims that's also "highly unlikely" — but here again, microbes cannot reveal their origin story.

As part of the larger "Operation Night Watch" team, van Bloois is definitely inspired by this "group effort where everyone is just really enthusiastic about telling these stories and adding to the knowledge surrounding 'The Night Watch.'".

The microbiological samples revealed by the laboratory process resemble abstract art in miniature: colorful clusters, delicate textures and intricate patterns created by living organisms.

And as the study is unfolding publicly, it also feels like an artistic performance of its own.

The project also perfectly embodies the full name of the museum where the exhibition is held: Natura Artis Magistra, a Latin phrase that translates to "nature is the teacher of art and science," as the microbiologist points out: "It's really cool to see science and art all come together in this project.".

The exhibition "The Night Watch Lives" runs at ARTIS-Micropia in Amsterdam until the end of May 2027.

Supporters of Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva are expected to be permitted to travel for their Europa League fixture against Bournemouth in January.

A previous decision to ban fans of fellow Israeli team Maccabi Tel Aviv from a Europa League game at Aston Villa last November caused controversy, with the move openly denounced by the then Prime Minister, Sir Keir Starmer.

That call prompted an investigation by the Independent Office for Police Conduct in August into former West Midlands Police chief constable Craig Guildford over allegations of gross misconduct.

Presently, Dorset Police are planning on the basis that Hapoel travelling fans will attend the 28 January match, though security assessments and intelligence reviews remain ongoing with two months remaining before kick-off.

Dorset Police’s Gold Commander for the game, Assistance Chief Constable Lindsay Dudfield, stated: "We are continuing to work closely with partners to ensure we can facilitate a safe and enjoyable match for all concerned.

"As with previous fixtures, we regularly review the latest information and intelligence to inform our policing operation and the resources required. All intelligence received will be carefully verified before informing any decisions we make around our plans.

"We are also in regular contact with interested parties in our communities to ensure we communicate clearly with them around what to expect and our policing intends for the fixture, as well as listening to any concerns they may have.".

The match between Villa and Maccabi last year required the deployment of over 700 police officers.

In a recent development, on Thursday, Hapoel’s encounter with Besiktas was interrupted following altercations involving police and supporters of the Turkish side. The fixture had been relocated to Georgia following recommendations from Turkish authorities, having originally been scheduled as a home game for Besiktas.

Reports indicated that Besiktas supporters displayed Palestinian flags alongside pro-Palestine banners before unrest broke out, forcing play to be stopped. Georgia’s interior ministry stated that 16 individuals were arrested and three officers suffered injuries.

The Turkish football federation described the actions of Georgian police towards Besiktas supporters as "unacceptable".

Denouncing the unrest and violence during the fixture, European football's governing body Uefa released a statement saying: "Violence, aggression, hatred and any form of provocative, discriminatory or extremist behaviour have no place in football.

Recent findings suggest that "Uefa competitions are founded on the principles of respect, fair play, integrity and safety. The events witnessed at the above-mentioned matches run counter to these fundamental values and to Uefa’s objective, enshrined in its Statutes, of ensuring that football matches are played in a spirit of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness.".

Uefa confirmed that an ethics and disciplinary inspector has been designated to investigate the incident.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the basement of a central London WeWork this week, FourFourTwo slipped on a VR headset and stepped onto a virtual pitch.
  • It felt like living inside an interactively playable game of Football Manager - or recreating Guy Ritchie’s iconic late-2000s point-of-view Nike advert.
